dedupe_keys.name: newcastle digital twin prototype for multi agency incident management by ambulance fire and police

description: This case study describes a prototype digital twin that helps ambulance, fire and rescue, and police services coordinate their response to incidents in a smart city. Researchers at Newcastle University in England first used a systems engineering approach with responders to find out why they rarely use the traffic, weather, CCTV and sensor data that cities already collect: the data are scattered in many formats, often not in real time, and hard to share between agencies. They then built a use case on Microsoft Azure cloud services in which stakeholders can see available resources, send automatic updates to one another and bring in location-based real-time weather and traffic, for example to reroute around a flooded road. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY in Scientific Reports (2022). Coverage is a city-scale prototype developed with UK emergency services. Caveats: a prototype, not an operational system; code and data are not stated as available; facts here come from the abstract. Simulation uses: requirements and data flows for emergency response digital twins, and a starting point for a shared incident data ontology. Related records: the FireCom digital twin in Austin (case_study-firecom-austin-urban-fire-smoke-digital-twin) adds fire and smoke prediction, and the EDXL-HAVE standard (data-oasis-edxl-have-hospital-availability-exchange) covers hospital status messages between agencies.

outcomes: Identifies why Category 1 emergency services rarely use smart city data (heterogeneous data, lack of real-time information, communication inefficiencies) and builds a cloud prototype that lets stakeholders view available resources, send automatic updates and see location-based real-time weather and traffic, as a basis for a future multi-agency data ontology.
